historical_growth.growth_rate_source: contracted media rights and event cycle, not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: No comparable multi-year series exists. FY2021-FY2022 are UFC only, FY2023 adds WWE from 2023-09-12, FY2024 is recast for the acquired businesses, and total equity is dominated by acquisition accounting and ~2.0bn of buybacks. The equity-CAGR selection rule does not apply.
historical_growth.notes: Comparable-basis revenue: FY2024 4,884.2 (Paris Olympics year), FY2025 4,735.2 (-3.1%), FY2026E 5,810 (+22.7%: UFC Paramount step-up, WWE ESPN/Netflix, Winter Olympics and FIFA World Cup hospitality). Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC less equity-award taxes): FY2024 358.1, FY2025 1,030.4; FY2025 includes restricted-cash inflows. Selected rate is the base case's 10-year revenue CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: The contracted step-up is real but already in the FY2026 base. UFC (Paramount, 7 years from 2026) and WWE (Netflix 10 years, ESPN 5 years) grow mid-single digits on escalators, backed by 15.3bn of remaining performance obligations. IMG and On Location swing with the quadrennial calendar: down in FY2027 after the Winter Olympics and World Cup, up in FY2028 for Los Angeles, at 15-20% margins. Renewals in 2030-2034 land at moderate step-ups. Adjusted EBITDA margin drifts from 40% to 42.5% as fixed-fee rights outgrow costs, with part of the gain shared with talent. Buybacks continue to be debt-funded, which changes the capital structure but not the enterprise value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Scarcity of premium live rights keeps repricing upward: Netflix does not exercise its year-five opt-out and the WWE ESPN (2030) and UFC Paramount (2032) renewals repeat something close to the last cycle's step-ups, with international rights (Latin America, Australia already added to Paramount) sold separately. On Location's Olympic and World Cup hospitality scales rather than merely cycling, Zuffa Boxing becomes a third owned property, and site fees from host cities and Saudi events keep rising. Margins reach 46% as nearly all incremental media revenue falls through.
scenario_narratives.bear: Distribution concentration bites. Netflix opts out after year five (2030) or renegotiates lower, a consolidating streaming market leaves fewer bidders at the ESPN and Paramount renewals, and UFC without domestic pay-per-view has no variable upside to offset it. Talent costs rise through fighter and performer reclassification or antitrust-driven pay settlements, IMG's agency and hospitality businesses prove structurally sub-scale outside event years, and margins fall to 37%. Leverage from debt-funded buybacks (net debt ~4.3bn including finance leases, with ~0.9bn more authorized) turns an operating disappointment into an equity one, and a controlled-company board has no obligation to change course.

valuation_philosophy.summary: TKO is valued as 100% of TKO OpCo's unlevered, fully taxed owner free cash flow, divided by all economic units (Class A plus Endeavor's Class B/OpCo units). That handles the Up-C minority once: Endeavor's distributions are its pro-rata share, not an extra cost. Growth is built from the disclosed media-rights contracts and the Olympic/World Cup hospitality calendar rather than from a three-year history that mixes UFC-only, part-year WWE and recast periods. The FY2026 step-up from Paramount is treated as a level shift already in the base, not a growth rate to extrapolate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Class A holders bear full corporate tax on their share while consolidated cash tax looks low (59.4 in 9M-2026); a model that taxes EBIT at the reported ~13% effective rate overstates value per Class A share by roughly a fifth
Reported operating cash flow includes On Location customer money (restricted cash up 604.0 in 9M-2026); reported FCF overstates distributable cash in event years
Terminal value is cap-bound in the base and bull cases; the result is sensitive to the multiple a buyer pays for sports IP in 2036
Netflix opt-out after year five (2030) and the ESPN/Paramount renewals in 2030-2032 fall inside the explicit horizon and drive the bear/bull spread

Debt-funded repurchases: every 1.0bn of buybacks at prices above intrinsic value transfers value from continuing holders; the model holds the count and net debt at the latest anchors and does not project further leverage
IMG/On Location margins (21% in 9M-2026 against 15% a year earlier) have a short, event-distorted record
Controlled company: Endeavor/Silver Lake's tax position and interests sit at OpCo level and can diverge from Class A holders'

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted ECONOMIC units of TKO OpCo: 72,440,231 Class A + 116,158,615 Class B (each paired 1:1 with an Endeavor-held OpCo common unit, exchangeable 1:1 into Class A), both from the Q3-2026 10-Q cover as of 2026-10-30, plus 1,050,895 RSU/PSU shares on the treasury-stock method (Q3-2026 EPS note). Held flat because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Class A alone (72.4M) is NOT the divisor: the flows are 100% of OpCo.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-09-30: equity-based compensation add-back 154.0 (9M-2026 119.6 per Q3-2026 10-Q cash flow statement and Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, which agree; plus Q4-2025 34.4) + taxes paid on net settlement of equity awards 17.5 (9M-2026 financing; Q4-2025 nil). TKO publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: ~4.3% 10-year Treasury + ~4.7% ERP at beta ~1.0 gives ~9% cost of equity; first-lien term loans at Term SOFR + 1.75% (5.51% at 2026-09-30, ~4.1% after tax) at ~10% of enterprise value gives ~8.5%. One WACC across all three scenarios: leverage, renewal and control risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not a second time in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) for finance leases: 258.6 of finance lease liabilities (19.0 current + 239.5 long-term) deducted once in the equity bridge, principal not deducted from the flows, renewal carried as ~0.3pp inside capex %. Operating leases (70.9) are excluded from debt because US GAAP operating lease cost is already inside Adjusted EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: Up-C structure, NCI charged once through the DENOMINATOR. Flows are 100% of TKO OpCo; the divisor is Class A + Class B (all economic units), so Endeavor's ~61.6% OpCo interest (4,884 of nonredeemable NCI at book) is a pro-rata co-owner, not a bridge deduction. 'Distributions to members' (455.6 FY2025; 580.9 9M-2026) are Endeavor's pro-rata share of OpCo distributions plus tax distributions -- the same cash per unit Class A receives as dividends and as corporate tax paid by TKO Inc. Deducting them from the flows as well would charge the NCI twice. Because consolidated cash tax (59.4 in 9M-2026) only covers TKO Inc.'s ~38% share, the model taxes 100% of EBIT at a full corporate rate (26%) so that each unit is valued on the after-corporate-tax basis a Class A holder actually receives. Only the 34.4 redeemable NCI in the UFC Russia subsidiary is deducted in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: sports/entertainment IP and media rights), plus the leases and NCI adaptations. First valuation of this ticker. FY0 = FY2026E at the midpoint of guidance raised 2026-11-04 (revenue 5,790-5,830; Adjusted EBITDA 2,295-2,315, ~39.7% margin); 9M-2026 actuals are revenue 4,504.1 and Adjusted EBITDA 1,755.5. Year 1 = FY2027. Timing: the balance sheet is 2026-09-30, so Q4-2026 free cash flow (~1.5-2 USD/share) is not in the model, roughly offset by FY2027+ flows being discounted as if FY2027 ended 12 rather than 13.5 months from the valuation date. CASH: unrestricted cash only. Restricted cash of 958.8 is On Location customer money for FIFA World Cup 2026 matched by 956.0 of other current liabilities and is excluded; the 604.0 9M-2026 build in it flows through reported operating cash flow, so reported_fcf here is TTM OCF less capex (1,723.5) EXCLUDING that 604.0 (Q4-2025 restricted-cash movement not separately identified). reported_fcf is levered (after ~270 of interest) and after only TKO Inc.'s share of tax; the projections are unlevered and fully taxed. Interest income not stripped: the company is in net debt. BUYBACKS: 1,164.5 TTM, funded largely by new term-loan debt (929.9 borrowed 9M-2026); the flat count is funded, but by leverage rather than free cash flow; ~936 of authorization remains and management intends to fund it primarily with additional debt. October 2026 repurchases (73.4 for 417,795 shares) are reflected in the 2026-10-30 share count and deducted from cash in the bridge. No tax receivable agreement liability is recorded. HISTORY: TKO has existed as a combined entity only since 2023-09-12 and FY2024 is recast for the Feb-2025 IMG/On Location/PBR common-control acquisition; FY2023 holds WWE for under four months. Multi-year CAGRs are not meaningful and are not used to set growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 -1%: UFC and WWE grow ~6% on contractual escalators (Paramount 7.7bn over 7 years from 2026; Netflix ~5bn over 10 years; ESPN ~1.6bn over 5 years), offset by IMG/On Location lapping the 2026 Winter Olympics and FIFA World Cup (IMG fell 31% in FY2025 lapping Paris). FY2028 +10%: LA Olympics hospitality. FY2029 -3%: Olympic lap. FY2030 +7%: World Cup year plus WWE ESPN renewal. FY2031 onward 3.5-5%: escalators plus the Paramount (2032) and Netflix (2034) renewal cycles at moderate step-ups.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 guidance implies 39.7%. 9M-2026 segment margins: UFC 56%, WWE 56%, IMG 21% (15% in 9M-2025), corporate cost ~-270/yr. Mix shifts toward owned IP in non-event years and fixed-fee rights escalators drop through at high incremental margin, partly given back to talent costs.
base.tax_rationale: Full-corporate-tax basis on 100% of EBIT: ~3.5% entity-level foreign, withholding and state tax borne by all units plus ~24% federal/state on the remainder. The 9M-2026 provision of 123.9 on 960.9 pre-tax reconciles to this with TKO Inc. owning ~38-39% of OpCo. No ramp: there is no valuation-allowance or NOL benefit in the base year.
base.da_rationale: 9M-2026 D&A 335.3, of which 247.2 is acquired-intangible amortization that runs off (Q3-2026 run-rate 93.0 a quarter); converges to just above capex. D&A matters here only as a tax shield.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20%, above the 15% default: three distributors supply most media revenue, Netflix holds a 2030 opt-out, buybacks are being funded with floating-rate debt, and Endeavor/Silver Lake control the board. Base 50%: the next four years of media revenue are largely contracted and guidance has been raised twice in 2026. Bull 30%, below the 35% default: it needs both renewal cycles and the Netflix extension to go well, plus IMG/On Location margins that have not yet been shown outside event years.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
